transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in to see me today?
Most days I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest. It’s like the old me—the guy who could talk to anybody and enjoy the day—is just gone.
How long have you been feeling this way—has it been a matter of days, weeks, months, or longer?
About eight months now. It started when the new regional manager began coming down on me and taking accounts I’d handled for years.
Have you ever had a period—lasting several days or more—where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than usual?
No, I can’t think of a time like that. I haven’t noticed myself being unusually up or needing less sleep.
Over these past several months, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in almost all the activities you used to enjoy, nearly every day?
Yeah. I used to look forward to bowling, working in the garden, taking my wife to gallery shows, going dancing. Now I just make excuses and stay home. None of it feels worth the effort anymore.
Before these past eight months, have you ever had another period in your life—lasting two weeks or more—where you felt similarly down, hopeless, or lost interest in things this way?
I don’t know… I can’t really think of another time that was like this.
Besides feeling down, have you been experiencing a lot of nervousness, worry, or on-edge tension about work or other things during this time?
I’m not really sure what you mean. I’ve mostly just felt down and not myself.
During these past several months, have you been feeling unusually worthless, guilty, or down on yourself, even about things that aren't really your fault?
Yeah. I keep telling myself I’m useless now. Like all those years taking care of clients and providing for my family don’t count because I can’t even handle this job anymore.
Have you had any thoughts of death or of hurting yourself during this time?
Yeah… I’ve had thoughts that my wife and kids might be better off if I just didn’t wake up. It scares me, because I don’t trust myself the way I used to.

Can you tell me how this has affected your ability to keep up with your job and daily responsibilities—are you still managing to work and get through your day, or has it become very hard to function at all?

It’s become really hard. I missed an important client presentation, which is not like me. And at home I’ve pulled back so much that my wife felt she had to bring me in—she didn’t think I was safe just carrying on like this.
Have you noticed changes in your sleep—such as trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual—nearly every day during this time?
Yeah. I lie awake replaying work, just staring at the ceiling. And when I finally do sleep, I’m up around three or four in the morning already worn out and dreading the day.
